Declared secret reaches a public sink. Secret secretKey influences ledger-write owner as raw data, contrary to the configured privacy policy. Disclosure permission does not remove this dependency.

Raw witness check gates a privileged effect. withdraw requires raw witness data from secretKey to equal ledger owner on every modeled successful reach. The guard covers 1 effect site: ledger-write withdrawals. Sole-gate coverage is unproven: another condition or implicit check is unclassified. At least one history lacks a modeled private-preimage check against preexisting ledger data. Equality alone does not demonstrate possession of a secret; review the intended authentication and protocol role.

Public commitment uses predictable randomness. persistentCommit commits private-derived input using statically known randomness, and its result influences ledger-operation picks.insert. This removes the protection supplied by secret, unpredictable commitment randomness; low-entropy inputs can remain guessable. Intentional deterministic commitments require review.

Declared secret reaches a public sink. Secret voucherSecret influences ledger-operation redeemed.insert as raw data, contrary to the configured privacy policy. Disclosure permission does not remove this dependency.

Ledger-bound private preimage is published. Private value from voucherSecret reaches ledger-operation redeemed.insert without a hiding transformation. A hash of this value is asserted equal to ledger voucherHash on the same potential successful path. Ledger operation data is public. If an untrusted observer obtains a reusable authentication secret through this boundary, secrecy is lost. An intentional reveal protocol may permit this flow.

Published hash has a small private input domain. answer_ publishes a direct persistentHash digest of answer, whose declared Uint<8> domain has at most 256 values. The modeled hash input contains one private source and may include public context, which adds no secret uncertainty. Hashing alone does not hide such a small domain. Intentional disclosure, reveal phases and public identifiers require review; no secrecy intent or actual entropy is inferred.

Passing a value to a witness does not constrain the witness result. Review whether this argument identifies the intended member; lookup indices or independently checked inputs may be intentional.
